message.content: I'll mortgage Connecticut for a cash buffer and keep the pink houses intact.
message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I have $26 and am not in jail. My holdings include a pink monopoly with three houses, plus two other properties with two houses each. Three railroads are mortgaged.

Mortgaging Connecticut Avenue for $60 would give me an $86 buffer. p2's railroads and two houses on Boardwalk and Park Place would cost $1,100 in rent. I cannot afford that.

Virginia Avenue with three houses costs $500. That is the main rent spike. p3 and p4 are in jail and will likely land on the pink properties once they are released.

I have already built this turn. Only Connecticut Avenue is mortgageable. Virginia Avenue is the only sellable property because it has three houses while the others have two, so I must sell from the highest pile first. Selling a house returns half its cost.

Mortgaging Connecticut Avenue now would give me an $86 buffer. It would also block p3 from completing the light blue set. The downside is a $6 interest charge to unmortgage later, and it still leaves me short against dark blues or three railroads.

Mortgaging Connecticut alone still leaves me $20 short against three railroads. Selling the third house on Virginia would return $50 and drop its rent from $500 to $150, but that would undo the purpose of the build. I am also checking whether jail sits before the pink properties on the board order.

The board order confirms that St. Charles Place is just one space from jail, followed immediately by States Avenue and Virginia Avenue. Players released from jail will land on the pink properties right away.

Rolling a 1 from jail lands on St. Charles Place for $150, a 3 on States Avenue for $150, and a 4 on Virginia Avenue for $500. p4 has $1,081 cash and a get-out-of-jail card, so they may pay to leave or use the card and land on the pinks. p3 has only $53 and is in jail turn zero, so they might stay there. With only $26 in cash, I am weighing whether to mortgage Connecticut Avenue now to protect myself.

The $86 buffer from mortgaging Connecticut Avenue still cannot cover the red properties. One house on Kentucky, Indiana, or Illinois costs $90 to $100, so I would remain bankrupt if any of those land on me.

I should mortgage Connecticut Avenue now. Having cash is safer than risking bankruptcy resolution, which could force me to sell houses at half price or limit my choices. This also preserves my block on the light blue set.

I am now considering a trade. p2 has dark blues at two houses and $195, so giving them cash would help them build further. p4 has $1,081 but incomplete yellows and greens; I could offer Connecticut Avenue to p3 for cash.

I rejected giving p3 Connecticut Avenue. They only have $53, so they could build light blue houses and threaten me with lower rent than my pinks.

I also checked selling mortgaged properties to p4. Pennsylvania is mortgaged but incomplete because Pacific is unowned. St. James is mortgaged too, and completing the orange set would require p3's Tennessee and unmortgaging. Neither is immediately useful.

I should not give p2 the B&O railroad, since that would let them collect $200 in rent. I am now looking for a trade that gives me cash without strengthening my opponents too much. p4 is rich and in jail, so they might pay to get out. I could offer my mortgaged Pennsylvania Avenue to p4 for cash, though they already rejected that deal.

I ruled out trading the B&O railroad to p2. That would raise every railroad landing to $200 and hurt me more than it helps them. I also dismissed offering my mortgaged Pennsylvania Avenue to p4, since Pacific is unowned and the set remains incomplete.

I will keep the houses and mortgage Connecticut Avenue with a quiet public message. p4 is unlikely to trade for cash because they have a get-out-of-jail card and $1,081. p3 has only $53 and one house on reds, so they may want to stay in jail to avoid landing on my pink properties.

p3 was just sent to jail and will likely stay there to avoid landing on the pink properties. p4 has a get-out-of-jail card and $1,081 cash, so they might leave immediately and land on the pinks. I should not warn them about the danger. My public message already warned them about the built pinks.

function.arguments: {"space_key":"CONNECTICUT_AVENUE","public_message":"Raising a little cash. Pinks stay as they are.","private_thought":"Cash $26 is too thin for even small rents or cards. Mortgage CT for $60 → $86. Still blocks p3 light blues. Do not sell the Virginia 3rd house ($500 spike) unless a debt forces it — p3/p4 are in jail and exit onto the pinks. Do not trade cash or B&O to p2 (dark blues 2-2; 4th RR would be $200). Do not sell pinks, St James, or PA. Next: end turn unless a clearly favorable cash trade appears. $86 still loses to 3-RR ($100), Illinois 1-house ($100), and any dark blue — sell Virginia back to 2-2-2 ($50) only if forced, rather than bust."}
